memories.memory: I send my younger sister about $300 a month to help with her rent, but I have recently started setting firmer limits because the arrangement is affecting my own retirement savings.

My closest friend of more than forty years and I stopped speaking for nearly six months after she criticized my decision to move across the country, though we slowly repaired the friendship over coffee last autumn.
In February 2024, I filed a formal complaint with the director of my community research nonprofit after a male colleague repeatedly presented my interview findings as his own during staff meetings.
I still do part-time social-services consulting three days a week, even though I could retire, because I enjoy mentoring younger practitioners and earning roughly $2,400 a month from the work.
I loaned a longtime friend $6,500 to keep her small counseling practice open during a difficult year, and we agreed in writing that she would repay me in monthly installments of $250.
My partner and I have lived in separate homes for the past four years because we both value our independence, but we spend most weekends together and are discussing a shared trip to Nova Scotia.
Last year I asked my supervisor to remove me from a project after a junior staff member was blamed for a reporting error that I believed resulted from unrealistic deadlines set by senior management.
